entry_conditions: Container and bowl poses are finite. Enter with the source upright and table-supported and fingers open, or from a nearby closed-low/closed-lifted state only when source/TCP co-motion is plausible. The source handle geometry must be unchanged and a collision-free reachable Panda configuration must be available.
exit_conditions: Observed fingers are closed, source and TCP have co-moved, the source is clear of the table, all particles remain in the source, and the upright source is staged at the demonstrated high relation above the bowl.
overlap_role: The full [180,360) interval is action-supervised here and in controlled_pour_and_right. It covers closed-gripper lift, upright carry, bowl-relative staging and the first small tilt, supporting early or nominal switching.
successor_readiness: Invoke controlled_pour_and_right only after physical observations support closure, source/TCP co-motion and clearance. Nominal readiness is the high bowl-relative stage; the decoder's destination weight alone is never sufficient evidence.
failure_signatures: Closed fingers without source/TCP co-motion, no source lift, a wrong phase weight around transition, abrupt or stalled transport, source slip/drop, early particle escape, an upright source outside the bowl footprint, IK nonconvergence, or joint-limit contact.
continuation_guidance: Preserve the two causal frames across switches and monitor finger width, source elevation and source/TCP motion. The source branch should dominate approach and low lift; the bowl branch should dominate clear-lift transport. Stop or select another policy if grasp loss or unreachable IK is observed rather than treating the phase weight as recovery logic.
limitations: Finger width and elevation are phase proxies rather than force/contact labels. Unseen grasp misses, slips, large rotations, changed geometry, noisy poses, obstacles and unreachable source/bowl placements are unsupported. Dual-frame supervision and absolute world orientation may underperform under the fixed training budget.
